apiKey.description: When the server configures an API key, every request must carry that bearer token except routes whose security array is empty.

apiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
apiKeyHeader.description: The Anthropic client header. Only /v1/messages accepts it, as an alternative to the bearer form. A request that sets it must match the configured key; a set key that is wrong, not readable header text, or one of several rejects the request without fallback.

Unauthorized.description: The configured bearer credential is missing or invalid.

BadRequest.description: The request fails schema or bounds checks. A bounds failure names the field in error.message.

NotFound.description: The requested model, engine, or session does not exist.

CapacityConflict.description: MemoryPlan or ContextLimit rejects the requested capacity. MemoryPlan returns code memory_plan. ContextLimit returns code context_limit when the prompt exceeds the position limit of the engine. The resident Flash-Next path allows 2,051 positions today, so a prompt of 2,051 tokens or more returns 409. The status is never 400. The server checks this limit before admission.

CheckpointFailure.description: A checkpoint or snapshot failed identity or load.

Overloaded.description: The bounded job queue cannot admit the request.

BackendFailure.description: Native initialization or model execution failed before response headers.

code.description: Stable machine code for the failure class. The mapping from EngError variant to code is normative and lives in the server design, section Error codes. Only the /ready handler produces not_ready. No chat route returns it.

id.description: Model name. Use this value in the "model" field of a chat request.

created.description: Unix time in seconds when the server started. OpenAI clients require this field.

engines.description: Engines that hold this model right now.

cache_budget_mb.description: Aggregate session-state reservation in MiB for this engine. All active and idle sessions share this cap, including KV, indexer, recurrent, auxiliary, history, and logit storage. Omission uses a cap derived from the engine memory plan.

quantize_kv.description: Store the key-value cache at 8 bits. The rope component of each key stays unquantized.

memory_budget_mb.description: Upper bound on memory this engine may hold. The server rejects the engine when the fleet plan cannot fit it.

expert_tier.description: "ssd" streams mixture-of-experts weights from disk. "resident" holds all weights in memory.

state.description: A native failure is process-scoped (decision 0022). When it occurs, every engine becomes native-failed, drains, and the process exits. The engine_state gauge uses the integers loading=0, ready=1, busy=2, error=3, stopped=4, native-failed=5.

kv_bytes.description: Key-value cache bytes now held in memory.

prefix_hits.description: Turns that reused a cached prefix.

snapshot_bytes.description: Snapshot bytes now held on disk for this engine.

persist.description: True writes a snapshot after each turn. The session resumes after a server restart.

tokens_held.description: Tokens the engine holds for this session.

model.description: Without x-session, route to the first engine that holds this model unless x-engine selects an engine. With x-session, a model that conflicts with the session binding returns BadRequest from Phase 2. In Phase 1, a request with x-session that passes authentication, body size, and schema checks returns NotFound before the model is checked. A request that sets none of model, x-engine, and x-session returns BadRequest.

temperature.description: The engine default from generation_config.json in the model directory of the engine that serves the request, else 0.7. A request that sets the field keeps its value.

top_p.description: The engine default from generation_config.json in the model directory of the engine that serves the request, else 1.0. A request that sets the field keeps its value.

top_k.description: The engine default from generation_config.json in the model directory of the engine that serves the request, else 0 (off). A request that sets the field keeps its value.

x-thinking.description: Maps to the chat template enable_thinking flag of the family.

stop.description: Stop sequences match on decoded text.

x-engine.description: Without x-session, this engine id takes precedence over model. With x-session, an engine that conflicts with the session binding returns BadRequest from Phase 2. In Phase 1, a request with x-session that passes authentication, body size, and schema checks returns NotFound.

x-session.description: In Phase 1, no session registry exists. A request with x-session that passes authentication, body size, and schema checks returns NotFound. From Phase 2, resolve this session and its engine binding. A missing session returns NotFound. From Phase 2, a conflicting model or x-engine returns BadRequest. Prefix reuse follows the cache rules, not unconditional processing of unheld tokens. Without x-session, create one anonymous session with empty private state. Release it after completion and GPU teardown.

strict.description: Requests typed argument values that follow parameters. Until the grammar packets of decision 0045 land, the server accepts this field and applies no constraint. The server parses tool calls from the output in all cases.

ResponseFormat.description: Output format. The type text is the default and applies no constraint. Until the grammar packets of decision 0045 land, the types json_object and json_schema return 400 bad_request. The server never ignores them silently.

ToolChoice.description: none disables tool calls. auto permits tool calls. required requires a tool call. The object selects one named function. Until the grammar packets of decision 0045 land, the server cannot enforce required or a named function. It returns 400 bad_request for both and never treats them as a prompt hint.

arguments.description: JSON encoded arguments. A completed call carries a JSON object as text.

ToolCallDelta.description: One tool call fragment in a stream. Clients group fragments by index. The first fragment of a call carries id, type, and function.name. Later fragments of the same call carry function.arguments only. A client concatenates the arguments strings in stream order.

index.description: Position of the call in the message. The first call has index 0.

arguments.description: A fragment of the JSON encoded arguments.

content.description: A string, or an array of text parts whose text the server concatenates in order with no separator. Null is valid on an assistant message that carries tool calls.

tool_call_id.description: Required when role is tool. The value is the id of the assistant tool call that this message answers. The content of a tool message is the result text.

total_tokens.description: The sum of prompt_tokens and completion_tokens.

reused_tokens.description: Prompt tokens served from the saved prefix state; 0 when a stop string ended the reply.

cached_tokens.description: The served prefix count, clamped to prompt_tokens (min(reused_tokens, prompt_tokens)); equals reused_tokens whenever the reuse accounting is consistent. prompt_tokens INCLUDES cached tokens (OpenAI semantics), unlike the Anthropic input_tokens contract.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Present by default; any ENGINESRV_CACHE_USAGE value other than the exact 1, true, or on removes it (the switch also governs the Anthropic cache fields).

content.description: Null is valid when the message carries tool calls. This field never contains the text of a think block.

reasoning_content.description: Optional extension. The text of the think block, without the think tags. The server omits the field when the reply has no think block.

tool_calls.description: Present when the model completed at least one tool call. Each call has a server generated id.

created.description: Unix time in seconds when the completion started.

model.description: Name of the model that served the request.

role.description: The first chunk of a stream carries role assistant. Later chunks omit it.

content.description: Never contains the text of a think block.

reasoning_content.description: Optional extension. A fragment of the think block text, without the think tags. Fragments come before the first content fragment.

tool_calls.description: Tool call fragments. The server sends no part of the tool call markup as content. A call appears here after the server has parsed it, with its id, name, and arguments. The final chunk carries finish_reason tool_calls when at least one call completed.

finish_reason.description: Present on the final chunk only.

created.description: Unix time in seconds when the completion started.

model.description: Name of the model that served the request.

usage.description: Present on the final chunk only.

id.description: msg_ followed by the completion id of the chat pipeline.

stop_reason.description: end_turn on end of sequence, stop_sequence when a stop string matched, max_tokens on the output limit, tool_use when an assembled tool call completed.

stop_sequence.description: The stop string that matched, else null.

input_tokens.description: With the split on (the shipped default; any ENGINESRV_CACHE_USAGE value other than the exact 1, true, or on — empty, 0, false, TRUE included — forces the legacy whole-prompt shape), the final usage — the message body and message_delta — carries exactly the prompt tokens not served from the saved prefix (the Anthropic contract EXCLUDES cached tokens from input_tokens), and input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens equals the whole prompt on every row the engine produces; a reader that consumes input_tokens alone then sees less than the full prompt — that is the contract, not a bug. message_start always carries the WHOLE prompt (the split is not known yet). After a stop string ended the reply the cache fields are 0 and input_tokens is the whole prompt.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Present by default; any ENGINESRV_CACHE_USAGE value other than the exact 1, true, or on removes it. Prompt tokens served from the saved prefix state; 0 in message_start (the split is not known until the job finishes) and on cold rows.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Present by default; any ENGINESRV_CACHE_USAGE value other than the exact 1, true, or on removes it; always 0 — the engine stores prefixes but never bills creation.

system.description: A string or text blocks. Plain string items are accepted as an extension and join like text blocks. It becomes a leading system message. An explicit null counts as omitted.

stream.description: Selects the SSE event stream. Null counts as omitted.

type.description: Adaptive is Claude Code's default: the model decides. It maps to enabled; the engine's own thinking control owns the budget.

content.description: A string, or an array of text, image, document, tool_result, thinking, and tool_use blocks. Image and document blocks become text notes. A tool_result becomes its own tool message in order. Assistant thinking blocks are dropped.

type.description: any and tool return 400 until forced tool calls exist.

max_tokens.description: Accepted and ignored. Validated like on /v1/messages (an integer of at least 1) and then ignored — count_tokens schedules no generation.

system.description: A string or text blocks. Plain string items are accepted as an extension and join like text blocks. It becomes a leading system message. An explicit null counts as omitted.

stream.description: Accepted and ignored. count_tokens never streams.

type.description: Adaptive is Claude Code's default: the model decides. It maps to enabled; the engine's own thinking control owns the budget.

input_tokens.description: The number of tokens in the prompt.

200.description: At least one engine is ready.

503.description: No engine is ready. Only this handler builds the body with code not_ready.

post.description: Set stream to true for server-sent events. From Phase 2, session routing preserves the session binding. The stream field selects the response media type. The server ignores Accept. Before response headers, all listed errors return JSON even when stream is true. A streaming response sends its headers and the role chunk when the server admits the job, before prefill starts. Until the first data event, the server sends the SSE comment line ": keep-alive" every 15 seconds. After headers, any error sends exactly one event: error whose JSON data matches Error (BackendError for a backend failure), then closes the stream without a success finish event, usage event, or [DONE]. A prompt above the position limit of the engine returns 409 context_limit before admission. The server returns 400 bad_request for response_format of type json_object or json_schema, and for tool_choice required or a named function, until the grammar packets of decision 0045 land. Client disconnect cancels the job. The server closes that stream without [DONE] and without an error event. A job whose bounded output channel is full with no reader is cancelled. The server closes that stream as on disconnect. No timeout applies. Tokens do not cross jobs. finish_reason is stop on end of sequence or a stop-sequence match, length on the max_tokens limit, and tool_calls when an assembled tool call completes.

requestBody.description: The chat body has a 16 MiB cap. Larger bodies return BadRequest.

200.description: One completion, or a stream of chunks.

schema.description:
Each token event has this shape:
data: {"id":"...","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1700000000,"model":"...","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"..."}}]}
The first event carries delta.role assistant. Later events omit it.
The server sends the headers and this first event at admission.
Until the first data event, the server sends the comment line
": keep-alive" followed by a blank line every 15 seconds.
Clients ignore comment lines.
Think block text arrives in delta.reasoning_content. It never
arrives in delta.content.
Tool calls arrive in delta.tool_calls. Each entry has an index.
The first entry of a call has id, type, and function.name.
Entries carry function.arguments fragments.
A blank line ends each event.
The final event carries usage. Its choice carries finish_reason.
finish_reason is tool_calls when at least one call completed.
A successful stream ends with data: [DONE].
After response headers, any error sends exactly one
event: error event whose JSON data matches Error
(BackendError for a backend failure). Example:
event: error
data: {"error":{"message":"Model execution failed.","code":"backend_error"}}
The server then closes the stream without a success
finish event, usage event, or [DONE] marker.

post.description: The Anthropic client path. A request carries the same bearer credential or the Anthropic x-api-key header. The body converts into the chat pipeline: system becomes a leading system message, text blocks join with a blank line, image and document blocks become text notes, tool_result blocks become tool messages in order, and assistant thinking blocks in history are dropped, because the chat template has no reasoning history. tool_choice any and tool return 400 until forced tool calls exist. With stream true the reply is the Messages event stream; a failure before the headers stays a JSON status reply even when streaming was requested, and a client disconnect or engine abort closes the stream with no error event and no message_stop. Capacity failures (memory plan, context limit) return 400 invalid_request_error, not 409: the Messages contract has no 409. The beta query parameter is accepted and ignored.

requestBody.description: The body has the same 16 MiB cap as the chat path.

200.description: One message, or a stream of events.

schema.description:
Each event is a named SSE event whose data holds one JSON
object. The sequence is message_start, then
content_block_start, content_block_delta, and
content_block_stop for each content block, then
message_delta with the stop reason and the usage totals,
then message_stop. The usage of message_start counts the
input tokens of the accepted request; message_delta carries
the final totals. A failure after the headers is one error
event in the Anthropic error shape, and the stream ends.
After any quiet 15-second interval, the server sends the
comment line ": keep-alive" followed by a blank line.

400.description: The request fails a schema or bounds check, or fails a capacity check. error.type is invalid_request_error.

401.description: The credential is missing or wrong. error.type is authentication_error.

404.description: The model does not exist. error.type is not_found_error.

413.description: The body is larger than 16 MiB. error.type is request_too_large.

500.description: Model execution or its checkpoint setup failed. error.type is api_error.

503.description: The queue refuses the job. error.type is overloaded_error.

post.description: The Anthropic token-counting path. A request carries the same bearer credential or the Anthropic x-api-key header and the same 16 MiB body cap as /v1/messages. The body parses the same way, except max_tokens is not a parameter of count_tokens: a body may omit it, and a provided value is accepted and ignored. The prompt renders and tokenizes through the same tokenizer path as the chat pipeline; no engine job runs and nothing streams. The reply is the input token count of the rendered prompt.

requestBody.description: The body has the same 16 MiB cap as the chat path.

200.description: The input token count of the rendered prompt.

400.description: The request fails a schema or bounds check. error.type is invalid_request_error.

401.description: The credential is missing or wrong. error.type is authentication_error.

404.description: The model does not exist. error.type is not_found_error.

413.description: The body is larger than 16 MiB. error.type is request_too_large.

500.description: Tokenizer execution failed. error.type is api_error.

409.description: The memory plan cannot fit this engine, or the context limit rejects the request.

422.description: The checkpoint failed identity or load.

delete.description: Stops the engine and frees its memory. Sessions that point at this engine stop. Snapshots stay on disk.
Drops all held prefixes and key-value state. Disk snapshots stay.

201.description: Session created. Phase 1 does not ship this route (the server design, Phase 1 session scope).

409.description: The engine lacks capacity for another session state.

200.description: The session. Phase 1 does not ship this route (the server design, Phase 1 session scope).

delete.description: Drops the held state and its memory reservation. Phase 1 does not ship this route (the server design, Phase 1 session scope). Deletes the disk snapshot when no other session references it.

| generate_seconds_total | counter | engine |
| tokens_out_total | counter | engine |

| draft_accepted_total | counter | engine |
